p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration of the transduction of the epinephrine signal; this part a of two drawings. Image a. An image of a yellow rectangular plane, with V-shaped tailes of a similar color. At the top and bottom of this plane are small blue ball; this represents the membrane. Above the blue balls on top is labeled "Outside," while the blue balls on the bottom is labeled "Inside." From left to right, there's a green snail-like structure with two projections into the V-shaped tails. The structure also has two curved tails that move from the projections to the right side and hold an ovular structure in place. The first of the two tails is labeled Gs gamma, the snail structure is labeled C closest to the bottom row of blue balls, to the bottom right of that is a grey horizontal oval with a GDP written on it, and below that is Gs alppha. The ovular structure is labeled Gs beta. To the top right of the entire structure just described, there's a pinkish-tan indented rectangular shape, labeled labeled beta-Adrenergic receptor, touching the top right of the green structure. The rectangular shape has pink and red loops inside; connected to one of the red loops is a small boulder-like structure with an arrow pointing to it from a similar shape. On of the red loops to the left is labeled N. This is step 1, which is described as "Epinephrine binds to its specific receptor." To the right of the green structure described previously, there's a green arrow pointing to the right to a green leaf-like structure with hairlike extensions all around it, attached to the bottom row of blue balls. The arrow pointing to this shape has an orange oval labeled GTP coming into the arrow (this is indicated by a curved arrow beneath it). Another arrow to the left of it curves downward to the right, pointing to the grey oval with GDP on it; this seems to be exiting the reaction. This is step 2, and the text associated states, "Hormone-receptor complex causes the GDP bound to Gs alpha to be replaced by GTP, activating Gs alpha.The green leaf-like structure described previously has the orange oval with GTP attached at its center, and below that is Gs alpha. The green structure is now attached to a blue tooth-like structure labeled "Adenylyl cyclase," which has hairlike extensions and is lodged into the yellow and blue structure. This is step 3, which reads, "Activated Gs alpha separates from Gs beta, gamma, moves to adenylyl cyclase, and activates it. Many Gsa subunits may be activated by one occupied receptor."Next to it is step 4, which reads, "Adenylyl cyclase catalyzes the formation of cAMP." Below the blue structure, a curved arrow starts from ATP to the left and curved down to a purple pentagon that has cAMP written on it. To the right of this is an arrow that points to step 5, which reads, "cAMP activates PKA." To the right is another arrow that points to text that reads, "Phosphorylation of cellular proteins by PKA causes the cellular response to epinephrine," this is step 6. The cAMP molecule described earlier has an arrow pointing down from it - the arrow has "cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase" written in blue next to it, and points to 5'-AMP. This is step 7 and reads, "cAMP is degraded, reversing theactivation of PKA."
